course_name_original: Radiação natural em materiais de origem geológica

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the sources of natural radiation
Quantify the radiation in materials of geological origin
Establish and characterize the exposure pathways
Assess the effects on health and the environment, by calculating doses
Framing and interpreting the results obtained in the framework of the applicable legislation
Present and communicate in an appropriate way the results of radiation quantification

syllabus_topics: Introduction to radioactivity and natural radiation
Physical description - radioactive decay, half-life, decay constant
Natural radioactive background and radioactivity of materials of geological origin
Exposure sources and forms of exposure
Current and relevant legislation and standards
Evaluation of health and environmental effects: dose calculation and biological effects
Forms of presentation and communication of results
teaching_methods: Lectures to expose the issues, with illustration of concepts, examples, and case studies
Biweekly assignments in an out-of-class environment
Short fortnightly quizzes in the classroom environment

assessment_methods.method: Final work with public presentation and report

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as 40% of component T plus 60% of component TF. Component T consists of biweekly work (35%) and short fortnightly quizzes (5%), while component TF is the final work with public presentation and report (60%). Eligibility requires attendance at least 75% of classes with mandatory participation in evaluation moments. Special assessment and classification improvement are conducted via a 100% weighted examination in a special appeal season.
